Here, ADMA (9,10-anthracenediyl-bis(methylene)dimalonic acid) acts as a chemical "trap" or sensor. When singlet oxygen is produced, it reacts with ADMA, destroying it. By measuring how fast ADMA disappears, we can deduce how much singlet oxygen was created.
The absolute method was employed instead of time resolved phosphorescence decay due to lack of standards for the modified fibres.

Since the fibers are modified and irregular, we lack a perfect "standard" to compare against. Therefore, we switch to the "absolute method," which calculates the yield directly from the chemical reaction rates without needing a reference standard.
